_comment: Phase 6 DORA dashboard. Deployment Frequency and (half of) Change Failure Rate are real PromQL against ArgoCD's own metrics (argocd_app_sync_total) — see Makefile's install-argocd target for the metrics.serviceMonitor flags this depends on. Lead Time and MTTR are documented as gaps, not faked: Lead Time (commit timestamp -> ArgoCD syncedAt) has no native Prometheus metric and needs a small exporter joining git log against the ArgoCD API; MTTR (alert firing -> resolved duration) needs the firing/resolved timestamps Alertmanager already sends to alert-webhook-receiver (Phase 4.3) aggregated somewhere queryable, which is a follow-up, not a single PromQL query. Change failure rate and MTTR are only meaningful because Phase 4's alerts exist at all -- that is the concrete justification for why Phase 4 came before this one.
title: DORA Metrics — app-a / team-a

panels.title: Deployment Frequency (successful syncs / day)
panels.description: Source: PLAN.md Phase 6 table — 'ArgoCD sync history / git commits to gitops/apps/**'. Requires argocd metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled (Makefile install-argocd).

panels.title: Change Failure Rate — sync-level (failed or errored syncs / total syncs)
panels.description: A proxy, not the full PLAN.md definition. PLAN.md defines change failure rate as 'Phase 4.2 alerts firing within 1h of a sync' -- a user-impact signal, not a sync-mechanics signal. This panel answers a narrower, always-answerable question (did the sync operation itself fail); the panel below is the closer approximation to the PLAN.md definition.

panels.title: Change Failure Rate — user-impact (SLO alerts firing, 1h window)
panels.description: PLAN.md's actual definition: a Phase 4.2 burn-rate alert firing within 1h of a sync counts that deploy as a failure. This panel shows alert-firing volume; correlating a specific firing window to the specific sync that preceded it is a manual read of this panel next to the Deployment Frequency panel, not a single PromQL join -- Prometheus has no native 'join by nearest prior event' operator.

panels.title: Lead Time for Change — NOT YET WIRED

options.content: **Gap, named rather than faked.** PLAN.md defines this as `commit timestamp -> ArgoCD syncedAt`. Neither Prometheus nor ArgoCD's own metrics expose a per-commit lead-time series -- `argocd_app_sync_total` counts syncs, it does not carry the originating commit's author-timestamp as a label. Closing this needs a small exporter: read `git log --format=%aI` for `3-tenant-workloads/team-a/gitops/apps/app-a/**`, pair each commit with the ArgoCD Application's `.status.sync.revision` / `.status.reconciledAt` via the ArgoCD API, and expose the delta as a histogram. Not built in this phase -- named here so the dashboard does not silently imply it works.

**Gap, named rather than faked.** PLAN.md defines this as `alert firing -> resolved duration`. Prometheus's `ALERTS` series has no `resolved` state to diff against -- it simply stops existing when an alert clears, so a bare PromQL query cannot compute a duration between two events, only observe the current state. The data does exist: Alertmanager already sends both the firing AND the resolved webhook payload (`send_resolved: true` in `prometheus.yaml`'s `alertmanager.config`) to `alert-webhook-receiver` (Phase 4.3), each with a timestamp. Turning that into an MTTR number needs those two events correlated and aggregated somewhere queryable -- e.g. a small script parsing the receiver's logs, or routing resolved-with-timestamp payloads into a table. Not built in this phase.
